(0) No attestation field. A gateway pre-consume makes the executor's consume a same-claim replay, which the executor accepts only with EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED. The gateway resume switch, the executor resume switch, the ledger, the executor fold writer, the session-core fold store and AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED (on both services) are one coupled flip.
(1) The switch is EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED (default false, strict `true`, mp_contracts::loop_fold::loop_resume_enabled, one parser, pinned by the_resume_switch_has_one_parser). With it off, a prerequisite off, or a ZDR or waived run, `loop` runs as `segment`: select_stage downgrades and never refuses.
(2) Order: consume (with effective_authority), the scope check, claim by `{run_id}:{consumed step}`, the pure fold checks, one ledger read, restore, apply_authority, a pre_effect fence at the claimed seq, the release pre-reserve, then dispatch. A failed fence or a failed pre-reserve in place is nothing dispatched: a denial at the fence is resume_forbidden (the same token as a denial on the claim or the ledger read), a ZDR refusal is the catalogue refusal, anything else is resume_checkpoint_unavailable.
(3) One release action per approval, `s{N}.tool_1_approved`, pre-reserved in both stages whatever its class, and even when its slot is rejected in phase 1. The release reservation is built by the same builder as a phase-2 reservation (run, action, tool, data category, zdr, class, digest), so session-core never sees two identities for one action. A second attempt ends continuation_already_consumed before any dispatch.
(4) A restore failure falls back to stage 1 under the same consume and never closes the fold.
(5) Absence is unknown. A recorded output wins for every tool, browser_agent included; the browser rule (NotResumableTool) applies only when no output was recorded. Withheld arguments are never redispatched (enforced in restore, not in closers::decide, which sees no arguments). A call refused before dispatch whose provider id is empty cannot be matched to its outcome, so the pause falls back. A paused step that completed or failed refuses; one left reserved or unknown_outcome falls back; NotRun on the original paused step is never fed to closers::decide.
(6) A PermissionDenied, Unauthenticated or ZDR-catalogue refusal from the claim, the ledger read or the fence refuses, and is never a fallback.
(7) continue_space_scope_unsupported is checked on the consumed snapshot; it is defence in depth while the gateway states no Space.

Operational rule for the coupled flip (this replaces the compose coupled-flip guard the design proposed: compose_violations already requires every switch_table row to be exactly `${NAME:-false}` on its service, so a second guard would add nothing). Flip together: EXECUTION_LOOP_RESUME_ENABLED, EXECUTION_EFFECT_LEDGER_ENABLED, EXECUTION_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED, SESSION_CORE_LOOP_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED and AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED. Deploy order: execution-core, then session-core, then model-gateway, then the BFF. Roll back in reverse, with model-gateway off first. What a mismatch does: (M1) gateway resume on and the executor's ledger off: the gateway's spend-only consume succeeds, the executor refuses the same-claim replay as continuation_already_consumed, the click is lost and the run waits out the renewed recovery window; the operator signature is the executor warn line continue_replay_refused_ledger_off (S7b step 6, not yet built) on each attempt with zero claims. (M7) gateway resume on and the executor's continue switch off: continue_disabled after the pre-consume. The other mismatches (executor resume off, checkpoint off, session-core fold store off) are harmless downgrades to stage 1. Compose pins the wiring per variable name only; it cannot pin that an operator sets the variables together or that an override file does not decouple them. Parser trap: AGENT_CONTINUE_AFTER_APPROVAL_ENABLED uses the lenient parser (1, true, on, yes) while the other four use the strict `true` only, so `1` flips continue on and leaves the others off.

findings.issue: The review finding asked that a resume whose writer is not Active downgrade to stage 1 instead of fencing. That is only half met. restore_in_place_with downgrades in one case only, a missing bearer (`let Some(bearer) = bearer else { return fallback(F::ClaimUnavailable) }`). For every other reason a writer is not Active, the implementer's hand-off sends the decision to agent.rs as a REFUSAL: names_for_later says 'A seeded in-place round whose writer is not active returns Refusal::CheckpointUnavailable.status() before building any fold'. save_fence on a non-Active writer returns Unavailable, which fence_refusal turns into CheckpointUnavailable. That refusal comes after the consume is spent and the claim is won. The row stays `resuming` (D3), so a retry inside the lease gets continue_in_progress, and after the lease the same refusal comes back. The run is stranded and the click is spent for nothing.
findings.evidence: restore_in_place_with has no input for the writer's gate state. Its only downgrade is `bearer: None`. The only test is restore_in_place_downgrades_to_stage_one_without_a_credential_and_makes_no_call. fence_refusal maps `_ => Refusal::CheckpointUnavailable`, which includes Unavailable{ambiguous:false}, the error from fence_with when !is_active(). The fold writer's gate (agent.rs ~1310) also turns the writer off for depth > 0, for resumed = ctx.release.is_some() (which step 9 must invert), and for StoreOff after a claim. select_stage and in_place_scope cover none of these. - New `in_place_writer_off(gate: fold::WriterGate, has_bearer: bool) -> Option<fold::OffReason>`. Disputed in part: the finding also names "StoreOff after a claim". That cannot be downgraded. A won claim proves the store was on; a store flip between the claim and the fence is a real store failure on a row that is already resuming, and refusing is correct there. `save_fence` still makes no RPC from a non-Active writer.

**A1.** `orchestration.proto` gains `ConsumeApprovalRequest.omit_call = 7`. The message previously ended at `claim_token = 6`, so 7 was free. The one `ConsumeApprovalRequest` literal in execution-core `agent.rs` (`prepare_resume`) gets `omit_call: false`; that is a single added line. `cargo check -p execution-core --lib`, `-p session-core` and `-p model-gateway` pass, and `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --keep-going` finished clean.

**A2.** All in session-core.
- **Store (`orchestration_store.rs`).** `ConsumeIntent { Full, SpendOnly }` is private. `consume_approval` keeps its exact signature and is now a thin wrapper, so the existing store tests are untouched. `consume_approval_spend_only` has the same shape.
- **No descriptor read.** A spend-only consume never reads or decrypts the descriptor on either branch.
- **Renewal.** `RENEW_RECOVERY_SQL` runs in the winning transaction only, and only for a spend-only consume. It touches only `open` or `processing` rows, scoped by `run_id` and `org_id`. It sets `deadline_at = now() + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS` and `next_attempt_at = now()`, and clears the lease. Zero rows is fine; a database error rolls the whole consume back.
- **`terminalization.rs`.** `MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS` is now `pub(crate)`, and the store imports it rather than keeping a copy.
- **`orchestration_grpc.rs`.** The handler picks the store call from `req.omit_call`. `consume_response(done, omit_call)` returns only the three flags for a spend-only consume. The `RunResumedAfterApproval` event is still tied to a won consume.
- **Descriptor reaper (review finding).** `approval_delivery` clears the descriptor of every approval whose `expires_at` has passed, consumed or not. A replay never checks `expires_at`, so while the descriptor stands it is answered. If the reaper has already run, the executor's full same-claim replay is now refused with `ConsumeRefusal::NotResumable`, which reaches the wire as FailedPrecondition `approval_not_resumable`. Before, it was a success with an empty call, and the executor then refused with the same token. A spend-only replay never needed the descriptor and is answered as before. The click is spent either way, and the renewed 15-minute window recovers the run. I did not edit the reaper (see deviations).
- **No single-writer assumption.** The new source scans cover `orchestration_store.rs` only. The renewal's comment names the managed-run start insert and the heartbeat as other writers of `deadline_at`.

**A3.** In `run_service_grpc.rs`, `RUN_SELECT` gains the `fold_pause_consumed` column (a CASE confined to `lc.kind = 'pause'`, alias `ap`, the LEFT JOIN still the last line). `RunRow` gains `fold_pause_consumed: Option<bool>`, with `None` added to all three test literals. `row_to_detail` now says: resumable = old rule AND NOT (fold kind pause AND consumed). `park_reason` is untouched, and `resumable` is still readable by every viewer.

Review finding on the descriptor reaper: I did not edit approval_delivery.rs (CLEAR_EXPIRED_CONTINUATION_DESCRIPTORS_SQL), which the review suggested changing to skip consumed approvals. A bare consumed_at IS NULL would leave a consumed loop approval's encrypted descriptor until the thread is purged, a retention regression, because loop approvals have no delivery row that would clear it. That is a behaviour change on one rare path: before, a call-less success reached the executor, which refused approval_not_resumable anyway, so the wire result at the executor is identical (FailedPrecondition approval_not_resumable). The click is spent either way and recovery relies on the renewed window.

The spend-only renewal uses the database clock (now()) rather than application time as the heartbeat does, and also sets updated_at = now(). It reuses the heartbeat's window constant MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS, which is now pub(crate).

WS03 S7c-A1..A3 (spend-only consume, recovery renewal, resumable predicate) - built, DB proofs written and not yet run.

- ConsumeApprovalRequest.omit_call = 7 (add-only). The executor's own literal states omit_call: false explicitly (no ..Default). A spend-only consume (store::consume_approval_spend_only) neither reads nor decrypts the retained descriptor on the winning branch or on a replay, and the response carries consumed, already_consumed and same_claim only. consume_approval keeps its signature and, for a full consume, its behaviour.
- A WON spend-only consume renews the run's managed terminalization obligation in the same transaction (RENEW_RECOVERY_SQL: state open, deadline_at now + MANAGED_DEADLINE_SECS = 900 s, next_attempt_at now, lease cleared; only open and processing rows; scoped by run_id and org_id; zero rows is not an error; a database error rolls the consume back). Reason: consuming the approval lifts the 'granted and unconsumed' hold the recovery worker honours, so a click spent after a long human pause would otherwise leave the run recoverable within about a second. The executor's own full consume never renews, so with the resume switch off the path is byte-identical. DB clock (now()) is used. NOTE for any future source scan: deadline_at has THREE writers (the managed-run start insert, the executor heartbeat, and this renewal); the earlier statement that the heartbeat is the only writer was wrong.
- Descriptor reaper finding (review finding 6): approval_delivery's CLEAR_EXPIRED_CONTINUATION_DESCRIPTORS_SQL deletes the descriptor of every approval whose expires_at has passed, consumed or not. After a gateway spend-only consume the executor replays in a later transaction, so expiry between the two can remove the descriptor. Resolution in the replay branch: a replay never consults expires_at (answered while the descriptor stands); a same-claim FULL replay that finds no descriptor is refused with the closed ConsumeRefusal::NotResumable (gRPC FailedPrecondition approval_not_resumable) instead of a call-less success; a spend-only replay is answered as before. The click is spent either way; the renewed 15-minute window recovers the run. NOT changed: the reaper itself. Open lead decision: keep the descriptor of a consumed approval while its run is non-terminal (add AND (a.consumed_at IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM runs r WHERE r.id = a.run_id AND r.org_id = a.org_id AND r.status NOT IN ('completed','failed','cancelled'))) to the reaper). A bare consumed_at IS NULL would retain encrypted action input until thread purge, because loop approvals have no delivery row that clears it.
- RunDetail.resumable (D5): resumable = old rule AND NOT (fold kind pause AND the approval keyed by pause_ref is consumed). Stage 1 consumes the pause approval and no longer closes the pause fold, so the fold stays claimable by state; the predicate stops RunDetail advertising it. resumable stays readable by every reader of the run; park_reason stays owner-or-service. RUN_SELECT gains fold_pause_consumed (CASE WHEN lc.kind = 'pause' THEN EXISTS(... ap.idempotency_key = lc.pause_ref AND ap.consumed_at IS NOT NULL) END); the LEFT JOIN remains the last line so the Space branch's appended JOIN still composes. Dependency: the pause approval is keyed run_id:step_id equal to the fold's pause_ref; if S6 or S8 changes that keying the predicate silently stops excluding consumed folds (costs a fallback, never safety).
- Verification status: pure tests pass (session-core 502 passed, 141 ignored). The #[ignore] DB tests (9 in orchestration_store::approval_consume_db_tests, spent_click_db_tests in terminalization, loop_checkpoint_a_stale_pause_fold_after_a_stage_one_continuation_reads_not_resumable in run_service_grpc) are written and compile but were NOT run; the lead runs them through scripts/tests/session-core-db-tests.sh with filters approval_consume_db_tests=17, spent_click_db_tests=1, loop_checkpoint_a_stale_pause_fold=1 (CI loop_checkpoint minimum 18 -> 19). Go bindings for omit_call not yet regenerated (buf, lead).

findings.issue: The new NotResumable branch in the replay path changes the FULL consume with every switch off. This breaks INV-13 and the spec's requirement that `consume_approval` keeps its exact signature AND behaviour (Full). The implementer says the wire result at the executor is identical. That holds only with the effect ledger on. With the ledger off, which is the default and the switches-off state, it is not.
findings.evidence: consume_approval_with, replay branch: `if same_claim && intent.returns_call() && !has_descriptor { transaction.commit().await?; return Ok(Err(ConsumeRefusal::NotResumable)); }` applies to `ConsumeIntent::Full`, which is the path the committed executor uses. Before this change, a same-claim replay whose descriptor had been reaped or purged returned Ok{consumed:false, already_consumed:true, same_claim:true, call:None}. In execution-core agent.rs prepare_resume, `replay_is_fenced = super::effect::ledger_enabled()`. With the ledger off, that response gave `failed_precondition("continuation_already_consumed")`. Now session-core's `Status::failed_precondition("approval_not_resumable")` propagates through `?` instead. Only with the ledger on did the old path also end in approval_not_resumable, through the missing-authority check. So the gRPC message token the executor emits changes with all switches off. The new refusal is also reachable without any gateway pre-consume: an executor retrying a consume after a dropped response, once the descriptor has expired and been reaped.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the NotResumable branch and keep the committed replay answer: a same-claim replay with no descriptor returns call None. The executor already turns that into the closed approval_not_resumable when the ledger is on. That is the only regime in which a gateway pre-consume, and so the reaper race, can happen. Keep the DB test, but have it assert call.is_none() on the full replay, plus the executor-side refusal. If the lead wants the session-core refusal anyway, gate it on the coupled switch so the switches-off path stays byte-identical, and record it in the ledger.

findings.issue: Design finding 6, the descriptor reaper racing the spend-only consume, is still open on the safety side. The executor's replay now ends in a closed refusal, which meets the letter of the requirement. But the user's click is still spent and nothing runs: after the 15-minute renewed window the run is recovered as outcome_unknown failed. The reaper itself was left unchanged and handed to the lead as an open decision.
findings.evidence: CLEAR_EXPIRED_CONTINUATION_DESCRIPTORS_SQL deletes the descriptor of every approval with `a.expires_at <= now()`, consumed or not. CONSUME_APPROVAL_SQL lets the gateway win right up to expires_at. The executor's full replay comes later, in a separate transaction. The reaper can run in between, and the replay then finds no descriptor. The DB test a_replay_after_the_reaper_removed_the_descriptor_is_refused_not_resumable pins this outcome; it does not prevent it.
findings.suggested_fix: Before the coupled flip, the lead should take the implementer's proposed reaper hunk: keep a consumed approval's descriptor while its run is non-terminal, by adding `AND (a.consumed_at IS NULL OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM runs r WHERE r.id = a.run_id AND r.org_id = a.org_id AND r.status NOT IN ('completed','failed','cancelled')))`. Alternatively, record in ledger.md that this click-spent-near-expiry window is an accepted risk, and add an owner and a DB test for it.

findings.issue: RunResumedAfterApproval now fires on the gateway's spend-only win, before RunAgent reaches the executor. Under D9 that includes the case where the connect is refused afterwards. The executor's later same-claim replay is not a win, so it never fires the event. The event now says 'resumed' at the moment the click is spent, not when the run actually resumes. It can announce a resume that never happens.
findings.evidence: consume_approval handler: `if done.consumed { broadcast_event(... RunResumedAfterApproval ...) }` is shared by both intents. After a pre-consume, the executor's consume returns consumed=false, already_consumed=true, same_claim=true, so no event is sent.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the changed meaning in the proto comment and the ledger entry. Or suppress the event for omit_call and fire it when the executor's same-claim replay succeeds after a spend-only win. The latter needs a stored marker, so it is probably a follow-up.

The single finding is fixed. It was real, and I fixed it test-first.

**What was wrong.** My `NotResumable` branch in the `consume_approval_with` replay path applied to `ConsumeIntent::Full`, which is the executor's own consume. Take a same-claim replay whose descriptor had been reaped. The committed code answered it with `Ok{consumed:false, already_consumed:true, same_claim:true, call:None}`. In `prepare_resume`, `replay_is_fenced = ledger_enabled()`. With the ledger off, which is the default and the switches-off state, the executor refused with `continuation_already_consumed`. My branch made session-core itself return `approval_not_resumable`, so that error token changed with every switch off. It was also reachable without any gateway pre-consume, for example an executor retrying after a dropped response once the reaper had run. That breaks INV-13 and the "exact behaviour (Full)" requirement.

**Fix.** I removed the branch from the replay path. A same-claim full replay with no descriptor is answered with `call: None` again, as committed. `read_consumed_call` already returns `None` for a missing descriptor row. The ledger-on path still ends in the executor's own `approval_not_resumable`, through its missing-authority check. The first-time-consume path is unchanged: its `!has_descriptor` check still returns `NotResumable`, as before. findings.issue: The HTTP effect table labels not_resumable and continue_disabled as approvalSpent 'no'. That is false in a normal retry flow. A client that retries after a dropped stream, or that double-clicks, can get not_resumable for an approval that was spent and whose run has since finished.
findings.evidence: continue_preflight in model-gateway sse.rs (continue_turn_gate, then terminal run_status -> not_resumable, only then approval_consumed -> continuation_already_consumed) checks the finished run before the consumed flag. A spent approval on a completed run therefore answers 409 not_resumable. CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_HTTP_EFFECTS maps not_resumable and continue_disabled to NOT_SPENT. chat-run-continue-contract.test.ts asserts 'no' for every pair except two. The continue_disabled gate also runs first, so a switch flipped off after a spend gives the same false 'no'.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not claim 'no' for not_resumable or continue_disabled. Give them an honest effect such as approvalSpent 'unknown-or-no', or document that the run is over and the approval may already have been used. Keep 'no' only for codes whose position in the preflight guarantees a pre-consume refusal, and test the wording.

findings.issue: The contract tells the client to 're-read the approval before any retry' (unflagged regime 2, reread:true, the 502 wording, the registry description, the client doc comment). No read the SPA has can show whether an approval was spent, so the instruction cannot be followed.
findings.evidence: model-gateway http_routes.rs approval_value serializes only id, run_id, step_id, kind, state, requested_of, decided_by and decision_reason, with no consumed_at or claim state. orchestration-client.ts normalizeApproval and the Approval type drop everything else, and a consumed approval stays state GRANTED. grep finds no SPA reader of RunDetail.resumable. The 'unknown' state therefore has no resolution path in the contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Either name the real resolution (resend the same token; 409 continuation_already_consumed means spent, which is safe because the gateway preflight refuses consumed approvals), or record a follow-up to expose consumed state in approval_value or RunDetail.resumable and name that read in the contract. Reword the description, the guard docs and the 502 text to match.

findings.issue: read_error_body returns Some(partial body) when the body read errors. Its doc comment says it returns None when the body 'fails to read'. No test covers a read error.
findings.evidence: `while let Ok(Some(chunk)) = resp.chunk().await { ... }` ends the loop on Err, and the function then returns Some(body) with whatever arrived. A chunked or content-length body cut after a complete JSON object is parsed and relayed as if it were complete. Only the 5 s timeout and the size limit yield None.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the chunk result explicitly: Ok(Some) accumulates, Ok(None) breaks, Err returns None. Add a test with a body that errors mid-read.

findings.issue: The BFF relay has no switch, so the /continue error vocabulary changes with every Model Plane switch off, which the byte-identical-when-off rule covers. continue_disabled, not_resumable and the other codes used to be model_error. The handler now also reads up to 4096 bytes of the error body, with a 5 s timeout, before it answers.
findings.evidence: CONTINUE_RELAYED_ERRORS is passed unconditionally from continue_run. Committed model-gateway with the switch off already answers 409 continue_disabled, which the BFF used to turn into model_error. A hung error body would now hold the browser request for 5 s.
findings.suggested_fix: Get an explicit lead ruling that this visible change is accepted because the SPA does not call the route yet. Otherwise gate the relay list on a BFF switch, so that off passes &[].

findings.issue: The gateway-parity half of the vocabulary test is not built. A doc comment claims a pin that does not exist. Nothing pins the SPA's 22 frame tokens to any source.
findings.evidence: The file holds only BFF=SPA HTTP parity and the &[] callers scan. orchestration.rs says CONTINUE_RELAYED_ERRORS is 'pinned against ... the gateway's list in tests/continue_error_vocabulary.rs', and the SPA test header says both lists are pinned on the Rust side. The model-gateway CONTINUE_HTTP_REFUSALS and CONTINUE_FRAME_REFUSALS constants do not exist yet (A4), and the frame list has no Rust pin at all. The deferred text is uncompiled.
findings.suggested_fix: Soften both comments until A4 lands. Land the deferred parity tests in the same commit as the A4 constants. Treat the frame vocabulary as unpinned until then.

findings.issue: A transport failure (502 upstream_unavailable, 504, a network error) gets no typed effect. Every guard returns null, which a caller cannot tell apart from 'this is not a continuation error'. The design review proposed an explicit class: spent unknown, followRun true, same-token retry resolves it. The only protection is the prose reading rule.
findings.evidence: chatRunContinueHttpRefusalOf returns null for {code:'upstream_unavailable',status:502}. The s7c-v3 review finding on the 502 case recommends a transport class in the HTTP effect table. orchestration-client.test.ts pins only that the result is null.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an exported transport-failure guard or effect (approvalSpent 'unknown', reread or same-token resend) so a UI cannot treat null as 'nothing to report' or as a free retry. Test it.

findings.issue: After continue_unavailable (ambiguous consume, no launch) the documented same-token retry may return 409 continuation_already_consumed. The contract then says approvalSpent 'yes' and followRun true, but no run was launched. The run stays parked until the renewed recovery window ends, about 15 minutes.
findings.evidence: The continue_unavailable comment says 'a retry either wins, or gets a 409 ... which means spent'. The design (D9, risks) accepts the strand. CHAT_RUN_CONTINUE_HTTP_EFFECTS.continuation_already_consumed has followRun true, and nothing says there may be no live run.
findings.suggested_fix: Say in the contract and the BFF message that after continue_unavailable a later 409 means spent but the run may not be live. Add a spent-no-run caveat or a followRun hint that is not unconditional.

findings.issue: The 'never echoes the upstream message for PermissionDenied or Unauthenticated' test uses a nested {error:{code,message}} body. The real grpc_status_to_http body is flat {"error": message}. The real shape is exercised only in the generic unlisted-body test, not under 401 or 403.
findings.evidence: http_routes.rs grpc_status_to_http returns json!({"error": error.message()}). The tests continue_keeps_every_other_upstream_error_closed_and_never_echoes_its_message and a_permission_or_auth_refusal_never_echoes_the_upstream_message build nested bodies with a code. The BFF never echoes a message in any shape, so the code is safe, but the comment overstates the coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 401 and 403 cases with the flat string body, including a message equal to a listed code token, and fix the comment.
